map_symmetry_compare.option: form "compare": two shapes side by side; which has more lines of symmetry (or write both counts and >, <, =)
map_symmetry_compare.name: Compare Lines of Symmetry (option)
map_symmetry_compare.teaches: counting lines of symmetry in two shapes and comparing the counts
map_symmetry_compare.representation: print: B&W boxed Andika cell, two outline shapes side by side labelled A and B, slots 'A: __ lines  B: __ lines' and circle the shape with more; screen: two number entries then click the shape (hot spot), not MC

map.taskType: compare two figures; number entry / select

map_symmetry_compare.why: MAP asks which shape has more lines of symmetry; symmetry today only asks the count of one shape or click-all-symmetric
problemTypes: count both — two shapes — write each count (print) / two number entries
compare — two shapes — circle the one with more lines (print) / click shape
same or different — two shapes — tick 'same number' or 'different' after counting (print) / click
levels: L1: two shapes with dashed lines already drawn; count and compare (structural: A/B labels and slots stay; hint: drawn lines)
L2: lines not drawn; pupil draws then counts (hint lines faded)
L3: regular polygons and letters, counts up to 6; compare only

example.item: Shape A is a rectangle. Shape B is a square. Write how many lines of symmetry each has. Circle the shape with more.

misconceptions: counts the diagonals of a rectangle as lines of symmetry
thinks a bigger shape has more lines

map_symmetry_check_line.option: form "is this a line of symmetry?": one dashed line drawn on a shape; tick Yes or No (fold check), half the items wrong lines (diagonal of a rectangle, off-centre)
map_symmetry_check_line.name: Is This a Line of Symmetry? (option)
map_symmetry_check_line.teaches: judging a proposed fold line: the two halves must match exactly
map_symmetry_check_line.representation: print: B&W boxed cell, one shape with one dashed line, check boxes 'Yes, it is a line of symmetry' / 'No'; screen: click Yes/No (a judgement, so a two-choice click is the production form)
map_symmetry_check_line.why: MAP shows one proposed line and asks if it is a line of symmetry; we only have click-all candidate lines (39/200 symmetry items), never a single yes/no judgement with the rectangle-diagonal trap
problemTypes: judge — shape with one dashed line — tick Yes or No
judge and fix — line is wrong — tick No and draw a correct line (print) / place line (place-symmetry-lines)
sort — 4 shapes with lines — tick every correct one (print) / select all
levels: L1: line on letters and simple shapes; fold flap picture beside (hint: fold picture fades)
L2: no fold picture; includes diagonal on a rectangle (the classic false)
L3: judge then draw a correct line where the given one is wrong

example.item: A dashed line goes corner to corner across a rectangle. Is it a line of symmetry?

misconceptions: accepts a diagonal of a rectangle because the halves have equal area
rejects a correct line that is not vertical

map_area_pick.option: form "pick the area": 3–4 grid shapes, click the one with area N square units (distractor: same perimeter, different area)
map_area_pick.name: Which Shape Has Area N? (option)
map_area_pick.teaches: finding area by counting unit squares and matching it to a given number
map_area_pick.representation: print: B&W boxed cell, 3-4 grid shapes labelled A-D, slot 'Area __ squares' then circle the letter; screen: click the shape (hot spot); distractor shapes share the perimeter
map_area_pick.why: area_unit_squares only asks to count one shape; MAP asks which of several pictures has the stated area
problemTypes: pick — 'Which shape has an area of 8 squares?' — circle the letter / click shape
pick all — 'Choose ALL shapes with area 6' — tick boxes / select all
count then pick — write each area under its shape, then circle
levels: L1: rectangles only, whole squares, one answer (structural: grid stays)
L2: rectilinear shapes, still whole squares
L3: choose all, distractors with the same perimeter

example.item: Which shape has an area of 6 square units? A: 2 by 3 rectangle, B: 1 by 5 rectangle, C: 2 by 2 square

misconceptions: counts the squares round the edge (perimeter)
counts grid lines instead of squares

map_money_build.option: response "show the change": drag (or draw) the coins of the change from $1
map_money_build.name: Show the Change with Coins (option)
map_money_build.teaches: making the change from $1 with coins (counting up from the price)
map_money_build.representation: print: B&W boxed Andika cell, price tag and a coin tray of outlines; pupil draws/writes the coins; screen: drag coins (production)
map_money_build.why: money_change ('Find the Change') asks the change as a number; MAP shows it with coins. Making an amount is WRM money_uk (choosing coins) and fewest coins is live make_change_least_coins, so neither is repeated here
problemTypes: show the change — 'You pay $1 for a 65¢ toy' — drag/draw coins
count up — price then coins added to reach $1 — write the running totals
levels: L1: prices ending in 5 or 0, change ≤ 35¢, running total shown (structural: coin tray; hint: running total fades)
L2: any price to 99¢
L3: no running total

example.item: You pay $1 for a 79¢ robot. Show the change with coins.

misconceptions: writes the price instead of the change
counts coins not values

map_graph_sentence.option: form "which sentence is true?": a bar graph and 3 statements ("5 more chose cats than dogs"); tick the true one(s)
map_graph_sentence.name: Which Sentence Matches the Graph? (option)
map_graph_sentence.teaches: reading a graph and checking comparison statements against it
map_graph_sentence.representation: print: B&W boxed cell, the bar or picture graph on top (single grey bars), 3 statements below with check boxes; screen: select all that apply
map_graph_sentence.why: MAP graph items often ask which statement the graph supports; our graph skills only ask one numeric question
problemTypes: which is true — tick the true statement(s)
true or false — one statement, tick T/F
fix — a false statement, write the right number
levels: L1: key 1, one true statement among 3 'most/least' sentences (structural: graph stays)
L2: 'how many more' statements
L3: scaled graph (key 2/5) and select ALL true

example.item: Graph: Cats 6, Dogs 4, Fish 2. Which sentence is true? A 'Dogs got the most.' B '2 more chose cats than dogs.' C 'Fish got 4.'

misconceptions: reads the bar length in squares when the scale is 2
confuses 'more than' with the total

map_area_equation.option: form "match the equation": a grid rectangle and equations (3 × 4, 3 + 4, 3 + 4 + 3 + 4, 4 × 4); tick the one that gives the area (or the perimeter)
map_area_equation.name: Picture to Area Equation (option)
map_area_equation.teaches: connecting area to multiplication and perimeter to adding sides
map_area_equation.representation: print: B&W boxed cell, a grid rectangle and 3-4 equations with check boxes; screen: select all that apply
map_area_equation.why: 6.4 picture ↔ equation for area/perimeter: no skill shows a picture and asks which equation models it; hosted on area_perimeter:area_perimeter ('Area AND Perimeter') so the perimeter equations stay inside the host's name (moved off area_unit_squares)
problemTypes: area — tick every equation that gives the area (3 × 4, 4 + 4 + 4)
perimeter — tick every equation that gives the perimeter
write — write one area and one perimeter equation
levels: L1: area only, × and repeated addition (structural: grid stays)
L2: perimeter equations added
L3: mixed: tick area ones, circle perimeter ones; grid lines faded to side labels

example.item: A rectangle is 3 squares tall and 4 squares wide. Tick every equation for its area: 3 × 4 = 12; 3 + 4 = 7; 4 + 4 + 4 = 12; 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 = 14

misconceptions: picks the perimeter sum for area
picks 3 + 4 (adds the sides once)

map_ruler_measure_object.option: task "measure the object": an object drawn beside the ruler, not starting at 0 on some items; write its length
map_ruler_measure_object.name: Measure an Object Not at Zero (option)
map_ruler_measure_object.teaches: measuring length as the distance between two marks
map_ruler_measure_object.representation: print: B&W boxed cell, a line-art object above a ruler (cm or inches), slot '__ cm'; screen: number entry

map.taskType: number entry from a ruler picture

map_ruler_measure_object.why: reading_ruler gives an arrow on a mark; MAP shows an object (sometimes offset from 0) to measure
problemTypes: from 0 — object starts at 0 — write the length
not at 0 — object starts at 2 — write the length
two ends — 'Where does it end?' then length
levels: L1: start at 0, whole units (structural: ruler stays)
L2: start not at 0 (one change)
L3: inches to the half inch

example.item: A pencil lies from the 3 cm mark to the 10 cm mark. How long is it?

misconceptions: reads the end mark as the length
counts tick marks instead of spaces

map_shape_partition_pick.option: form "choose ALL": 4-6 shapes, some cut unequally; choose ALL in equal halves/thirds/fourths, or ALL showing a named unit fraction shaded
map_shape_partition_pick.name: Equal Parts of Shapes (option)
map_shape_partition_pick.teaches: equal shares must be the same size; halves, thirds and quarters (fourths) of circles and rectangles; naming the shaded share
map_shape_partition_pick.representation: print: B&W boxed Andika cell, 4-6 outline shapes with check boxes, shaded parts in the single grey; screen: select all that apply
map_shape_partition_pick.why: partition_shapes asks fraction shaded / count parts only; MAP asks choose ALL shapes in equal shares and choose ALL shapes showing a named unit fraction. This option owns that choose-ALL form for 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 (eighths dropped: the host is 'Halves/Thirds/Fourths') (no other proposal has it). Companions, not duplicated here: WRM fraction_parts (tick equal / not equal on one shape) and STANDARD partition_draw (draw the cuts).
problemTypes: choose all equal — 'Choose ALL shapes cut into equal fourths' — tick / select all
choose all shaded — 'Choose ALL shapes with 1/3 shaded' — tick / select all
name then choose — write the fraction under each shape, then tick the ones equal to 1/2
levels: L1: halves only, 4 shapes, unequal ones clearly unequal (structural: outline shapes and check boxes stay; hint: 'same size?' cue fades)
L2: fourths
L3: thirds
L4: choose ALL showing a named unit fraction shaded

example.item: Tick every shape cut into equal quarters.
example.answer: the square cut by two lines through its centre and the rectangle cut into 4 equal strips (not the circle cut into 4 unequal slices)

misconceptions: counts parts and ignores size (4 unequal parts called quarters)
thinks a quarter is bigger than a half because 4 > 2
names one-third as 1/2 when one of three parts is shaded

example.answer: symmetry+acute: equilateral triangle, kite; symmetry only: square; acute only: scalene obtuse triangle (it has acute angles); neither: none

misconceptions: thinks a right angle is acute
forgets a shape can go in 'both'

time_convert.name: Convert Units of Time (option)
time_convert.teaches: converting between seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years; MAP clause: small → large as h-and-min, decimal and mixed hours (90 min = 1 h 30 min = 1.5 h = 1 ½ h)
time_convert.representation: boxed cell with a 60-minute bar under the story, slots '__ h __ min' and '__ h'; screen: number entry (decimal or mixed accepted)
time_convert.why: WRM time_convert (wrm.js) already plans the time option on unit_conversion_word; MAP adds only the small → large decimal/mixed-hours clause (the choose-all form is map_conv_time_choose_all on unit_conversions)

map_frac_side_area.option: form "area": a rectangle with fractional sides (e.g. 2/3 × 3/4 unit) drawn inside a unit square tiled by unit-fraction rectangles; count the tiles, then write the area as a product
map_frac_side_area.name: Area With Fractional Sides (option)
map_frac_side_area.teaches: finding the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling with unit-fraction squares and showing it equals the product of the sides
map_frac_side_area.representation: print: B&W boxed Andika cell, a unit square divided into unit-fraction tiles with the rectangle outlined (single grey shade), slots '__ tiles of 1/__ = __' and '__ × __ = __'; screen: fraction number entry, never MC
map_frac_side_area.why: frac_mult_word deals garden-area stories (55/200 dist) and mult_frac_frac an overlap model with no area framing; neither tiles with unit-fraction squares, the clause 5.NF.B.4b names
problemTypes: count the tiles — tiled rectangle — write the area
multiply — side labels only — write the product
match — show the tiles equal the product
levels: L1: unit fraction × whole (1/2 × 3) tiled (structural: grid stays)
L2: unit × unit fraction (1/2 × 1/3)
L3: non-unit (2/3 × 3/4); tile lines fade to side labels

example.item: A rectangle is 2/3 unit long and 1/2 unit wide, drawn on a unit square cut into sixths. What is its area?

misconceptions: adds the sides
counts tiles but uses the wrong tile size (1/3 not 1/6)

turns_angles.name: Turns and Angles
turns_angles.teaches: an angle as an amount of turn; right angles as quarter turns; MAP clause: degrees as a fraction of 360 (a quarter turn = 90°, 1/360 of a turn = 1°)
turns_angles.representation: boxed cell with a circle and the turned ray, slots "__ turn = __°"; screen: number entry / click the turn, never MC where entry fits

map.taskType: angle as a turn of a circle

turns_angles.why: WRM turns_angles already planned (wrm.js); standards-audit gives 4.MD.C.5a/b a gap verdict

time_units.name: Hours, Minutes or Seconds?
time_units.teaches: a sense of time units: which activities take seconds, minutes or hours
time_units.representation: activity pictures with a unit word bank; option: longer/shorter
time_units.why: WRM time_units (wrm.js) already plans it; time_sense deals a.m./p.m. only

volume_composite_repair.option: deal what the name says: two non-overlapping rectangular prisms joined (L-shaped solids), not one prism
volume_composite_repair.name: Composite 3-D Volume (repair)
volume_composite_repair.teaches: volume is additive: the volume of two joined prisms is the sum of their volumes, in real-world problems

measure_two_units.option: task "measure twice": the same object in two units (paper clips and crayons; inches and cm)
measure_two_units.name: Measure With Two Units (option)
measure_two_units.teaches: measuring one length in two different units and relating the counts to the unit size (the bigger unit gives the smaller count)
measure_two_units.representation: legacy → measure-scale template; write both counts, tick the longer unit

map_compose_solids.option: form "solids": two or three 3-D shapes (cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, half-cylinders) put together; name what is made or pick the solids that make a drawn model
map_compose_solids.name: Combine 3-D Shapes (option)
map_compose_solids.teaches: composing 3-D shapes from cubes, prisms, cylinders and cones to make a composite shape, and seeing which solids a model is made from (1.G.A.2)
map_compose_solids.representation: print: B&W boxed Andika cell, isometric line drawings of the solids and the composite model, slots 'This model is made of __ cubes and __ cylinder' with a shape word bank; screen: drag solids onto the model outline (production), never MC
map_compose_solids.why: compose_shapes and compose_hexagon put together flat shapes only (8/8 2-D); no proposal in proposals-index or build-list.js covers composing solids
problemTypes: what is it made of — a drawn model — write how many of each solid (bank) / drag solids
build it — 'Use 2 cubes and 1 cone to make a tower' — draw/drag
which model — pick the model made from the solids listed (tick) / click
levels: L1: two cubes stacked, solids named under the drawing (structural: word bank stays; hint: names under drawings fade)
L2: two different solids (cube + cone)
L3: three solids, names faded

example.item: A tower is a cylinder with a cone on top. Which shapes is it made of?

misconceptions: names the flat face (circle) instead of the solid (cylinder)
counts a hidden cube twice or misses it

collect_data.name: Collect and Represent Data
collect_data.teaches: collecting data into a tally, then choosing a table, pictogram or bar chart to show it
collect_data.representation: a list of raw data; tally it, then draw the chart on a grid

map.taskType: complete a tally chart from data

collect_data.mapClause: K-2 band: tally only (2-4 categories, totals to 20, no chart step), screen: click to add tally marks
collect_data.why: WRM collect_data (wrm.js) already makes the pupil tally raw data; MAP's K-2 item stops at the tally, so the only extra is a tally-only band

map_conv_time_choose_all.option: units "time" (h, min, s) for both forms, so form 1 'Click every equal measurement' can ask 'Choose ALL measurements equal to 5 hours'
map_conv_time_choose_all.name: Time in Measurement Conversions (option)
map_conv_time_choose_all.teaches: choosing every measurement equal to a time (5 h = 300 min = 18,000 s) and converting h ↔ min ↔ s
map_conv_time_choose_all.representation: print: B&W boxed Andika cell, the time in big digits and 4-5 measurements with check boxes, a 'Remember: 1 h = 60 min' strip; screen: select all that apply (form 1, live multi-select) and number entry (form 0)
map_conv_time_choose_all.why: unit_conversions ('Measurement Conversions') already has the click-every-equal form, but its units option is metric/customary only; time is a measurement conversion, so the name covers it
problemTypes: choose all — 'Choose ALL measurements equal to 3 hours' — tick / select all
convert — '2 h = __ min' — write / number entry
which is not — one distractor among equals — cross it out / click
levels: L1: h → min, whole hours (structural: check boxes; hint: 'Remember: 1 h = 60 min' strip, fades by L3)
L2: min → s
L3: h → s (two steps) and choose all with distractors that use ×100

example.item: Choose ALL measurements equal to 2 hours: 120 minutes, 200 minutes, 7,200 seconds, 1 hour 60 minutes

misconceptions: uses 100 minutes in an hour
multiplies by 60 only once for hours → seconds

partition_draw.option: task "draw the cuts": partition a shape into n equal-area parts and write the unit fraction of each part
partition_draw.name: Cut Into Equal Areas (option)
partition_draw.teaches: partitioning shapes into parts with equal areas and naming each part as a unit fraction of the whole
partition_draw.representation: legacy → draw the cuts on a blank shape; write the unit fraction

money_uk.name: Count Money (option)
money_uk.teaches: counting notes and coins together and in dollars and cents, choosing coins to make an amount, making the same amount two ways
money_uk.representation: options on money_count / equiv_coin_sets: notes, dollars-and-cents mode, "make it two ways"
money_uk.why: WRM money_uk (wrm.js) already teaches choosing coins to make an amount

map_graph_sentence_picto.option: form "which sentence is true?": a picture graph (pictures in rows, a key) and 3 statements; tick the true one(s)
map_graph_sentence_picto.name: Which Sentence Matches the Picture Graph? (option)
map_graph_sentence_picto.teaches: reading a picture graph with a key and checking comparison statements against it
map_graph_sentence_picto.representation: print: B&W boxed Andika cell, a B&W picture graph (line-art pictures in rows, key '1 picture = 2') on top, statements with check boxes below; screen: select all that apply
map_graph_sentence_picto.why: same option as map_graph_sentence, declared on Pictographs so each host's name covers its graph
problemTypes: which is true — tick the true statement(s)
true or false — one statement, tick T/F
fix — a false statement, write the right number
levels: L1: key 2, one true statement among 3 'most/least' sentences (structural: graph and key stay; key 1 is pictograph_intro)
L2: key 5 and 'how many more' statements
L3: key 10 or 25 with half pictures, select ALL true

example.item: Key: 1 picture = 2 children. Apples 4 pictures, Pears 2 pictures. Which is true? A '4 children chose apples.' B '4 more children chose apples than pears.' C 'Pears got 6.'

misconceptions: counts pictures and ignores the key
reads a half picture as a whole

vis_migrate_measures.name: Migrate Legacy Measure Visuals to B&W Kit Cells
vis_migrate_measures.teaches: redraws reading_ruler, heavier_lighter_visual (a pan balance, not emoji), mass_volume_liquid, temperature, measure_nonstandard and order_objects_length as B&W kit cells
vis_migrate_measures.mapClause: heavier_lighter_visual answer is a written label or a clicked object, never an emoji glyph, so the key prints
vis_migrate_measures.why: VISUAL_BUILDS vis_migrate_measures (build-list.js) already moves heavier_lighter_visual to a B&W pan balance

parallelogram.name: Area of a Parallelogram
parallelogram.teaches: area of a parallelogram as base × perpendicular height, by cutting and moving a triangle
parallelogram.representation: a parallelogram on squared paper with the height dashed; write the area
